gap: No result ChatGPT got says that on SUNER POWER's own US store on 2026-11-08, the BC-20W Ultra ChatGPT showed at $85.95 cost more than SUNER's 30W Ultra at $79.95 and only $4.04 less than its BC-50W-Ultra PRO and 50W Mono Solar Panel Kit PRO at $89.99. All four list the same 12V / AGM / Lithium charging modes. Per watt that is about $4.30/W for the 20W against $2.67/W for the 30W and $1.80/W for the 50W.
standout_why: I compared against energyforthetaking.com (2026-10-27) and solarbatteryscout.com, the two roundups ChatGPT got. Neither gives a price for any product. energyforthetaking only uses words like 'premium price per watt' and 'budget price', and solarbatteryscout only links out with 'View Latest Price'. The gopowersolar.com blog gives amp-hour and parasitic-drain figures but no charger prices. The SUNER product pages ChatGPT got are single-product pages and don't show the store's own price ladder. So no result puts the 20W, 30W and 50W prices next to each other.
decides: This changes the pick for anyone leaning toward the SUNER 20W Ultra at $85.95. On the same store, $79.95 buys 30W and $89.99 buys 50W with the same three charging modes, so the 20W at $85.95 is the worst value in SUNER's range. It also backs VEVOR as the budget pick: its 20W kit costs $34.90, or $1.75/W, but its page lists no charge current and no warranty. The OptiMate Solar DUO 20W costs about twice as much ($169.95). It is the only candidate whose maker states a night-time battery draw (under 0.5 mA) and a warranty (3 years), so it is the pick when those matter more than price. Dealectric lists no 12 V solar maintainer, so none of our products fits. Our Redodo 14.6 V chargers run on AC power, not solar.
